LESSON: JOHN THE BAPTIST TO THE MESSIAH

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Early life of Jesus Christ
Topic 4.2: John the Baptist to the Messiah

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on John the Baptist to the Messiah. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is John the Baptist a precursor to the Messiah?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18
2. apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: JOHN THE BAPTIST TO THE MESSIAH
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
John the Baptist to the Messiah helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: JOHN THE BAPTIST TO THE MESSIAH
Study John the Baptist to the Messiah like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “John the Baptist to the Messiah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to John the Baptist to the Messiah in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what John the Baptist to the Messiah is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “John the Baptist to the Messiah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to John the Baptist to the Messiah in your own words. (skill: apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach John the Baptist to the Messiah to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18.
3. Practise this skill: apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life.
4. Make one local Kenya example of John the Baptist to the Messiah from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for John the Baptist to the Messiah: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study John the Baptist to the Messiah?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is John the Baptist a precursor to the Messiah?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what John the Baptist to the Messiah means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss the message of John the Baptist in Luke 3:7-18.
5. Be able to: apply values acquired from the teachings of John the Baptist in daily life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
